reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure emerges from a bipartite interaction model between merchants and associates. The referral tracking kernel acts as a stochastic process mapping clicks to purchases, governed by a conditional probability P(purchase|referral). This induces a reward function W(R) = r * R where r represents the expected value per referral. The merchant distribution network forms a weighted graph where nodes represent associates and edges denote referral paths. Each node contributes to global exposure E through local influence weights. The system exhibits a dual nature: probabilistic inference in GSI for predicting conversion likelihoods, and dynamic state transitions in GSE for managing affiliate engagement. Failure modes arise when referral tracking breaks down (session loss), or when the compensation model underestimates marginal utility of additional referrals. The architecture supports recursive expansion of the network while maintaining bounded complexity through automated credit mechanisms.
